reference: GNU sleep independently checks successful finite-duration request status/output, not elapsed precision. Argument-error contracts follow the public clock API. Independent Python clock_gettime_ns samples bracket read-only clock reads and since arithmetic. Deterministic injected values, exact nanosecond precision and syscall failures still require mocks.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and help documentation for the five advertised subcommands
GNU sleep parity for zero duration, fractional scaling, and a one-nanosecond decimal input
Deferred controlled-clock verification for clock domains, since arithmetic, and interrupted syscall paths
Argument rejection and read-only monotonic formatting/order invariants; no elapsed-time accuracy claim.
Independent Python bounds for now/mono/boot reads and since subtraction.
exclusions: Injected clock-domain sentinels and forced nanosecond-borrow/zero boundaries require fixed mock samples; live independent bracket coverage executes separately.
Sleep precision, interruptions and injected syscall errors remain unverified.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash classifies bashclock as an enabled builtin.
Verify help exposes each subcommand and its documented clock or sleep role without invoking a clock operation.
cases.script:
h=$(help bashclock)
[[ $h == *'CLOCK_REALTIME'* ]]
[[ $h == *'CLOCK_MONOTONIC'* ]]
[[ $h == *'CLOCK_BOOTTIME'* ]]
[[ $h == *'since T0'* ]]
[[ $h == *'clock_nanosleep'* ]]
printf 'help covers now mono boot since sleep\n'
cases.stdout: help covers now mono boot since sleep

cases.purpose: Compare a zero-length request with GNU sleep; this exercises successful parsing and the zero-duration syscall path without relying on elapsed-time measurements.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashclock) == builtin ]]; then
  bashclock sleep 0.000000000
else
  sleep 0.000000000
fi

cases.purpose: Compare a fractional duration with GNU sleep, covering a fraction shorter than nine digits that must be scaled to nanoseconds.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashclock) == builtin ]]; then
  bashclock sleep 0.0025
else
  sleep 0.0025
fi

cases.purpose: Compare the smallest positive decimal duration supported by the documented nanosecond format with GNU sleep.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashclock) == builtin ]]; then
  bashclock sleep 0.000000001
else
  sleep 0.000000001
fi

cases.purpose: Verify deterministic clock-domain sentinels and special timestamp boundaries using injected readings.
cases.reason: clock_gettime is served by the vDSO in both builds, so seccomp cannot intercept it; deterministic sample injection needs a build-time test hook or ptrace/vDSO interposition. A user+time namespace (unprivileged in the VM plain driver if user namespaces are enabled) can offset CLOCK_MONOTONIC and CLOCK_BOOTTIME by chosen amounts but not CLOCK_REALTIME. Domain identity is closable unprivileged with a time namespace; boundary sentinels need a clock-injection capability.

cases.purpose: Force since subtraction boundary values and nanosecond borrow using injected monotonic samples; live independent bounds and ordinary argument errors execute separately.
cases.reason: Live brackets and argument errors execute. Borrow and future-START cases are forceable with crafted START values; exact zero and read errors need injection.

cases.purpose: Check clock_nanosleep EINTR handling and non-EINTR syscall error diagnostics.
cases.reason: EINTR is observable now, and a distinct clock_nanosleep failure is reachable with a stateless per-side seccomp RET_ERRNO filter. Neither needs a new driver.

Bracket read-only now/mono/boot and since results between independent Python clock_gettime_ns samples of the documented clock domain. Validate fixed-width formatting and elapsed subtraction without a frozen clock or timing-precision claim.
cases.script:
cat > clock_observer.py <<'PY'
import re, sys, time
domain = getattr(time, 'CLOCK_' + sys.argv[1])
if len(sys.argv) == 2:
    print(time.clock_gettime_ns(domain))
else:
    before, rendered, after, origin = sys.argv[2:]
    assert re.fullmatch(r'-?[0-9]+\.[0-9]{9}', rendered), rendered
    seconds, nanos = rendered.split('.')
    value = int(seconds) * 10**9 + int(nanos)
    assert int(before) - int(origin) <= value <= int(after) - int(origin), (before, rendered, after, origin)
PY
for mode in now mono boot since; do
  case $mode in now) clock=REALTIME;; boot) clock=BOOTTIME;; *) clock=MONOTONIC;; esac
  before=$(/usr/bin/python3 clock_observer.py "$clock")
  origin=0
  if [[ $mode == since ]]; then
    origin=987654321
    value=$(bashclock since 0.987654321)
  else
    value=$(bashclock "$mode")
  fi
  after=$(/usr/bin/python3 clock_observer.py "$clock")
  /usr/bin/python3 clock_observer.py "$clock" "$before" "$value" "$after" "$origin"
done
printf 'read-only clock bounds verified\n'
